correctness.rationale: Condition on the last reset age (density r exp(-rt)); the no-reset contribution has trace norm bounded by exp(-rt), and the integral of rank-one projectors gives the unique stationary state. The product free probabilities give the product overlap S(t,s)^d. All integrands in the overlap/Green representation are nonnegative, so Tonelli and monotone convergence apply even when the limit is infinite. For B(t)=ΣJ_n(2κt)^4, Parseval of the characteristic function gives its angular J_0² average. In Step 2 interpret the sine inequality on 0≤θ≤π after using evenness, equivalently |sin(θ/2)|≥|θ|/π; the literal signed inequality on negative angles is a typo. Integrating (1+κt θ)⁻¹ gives the stated logarithmic bound. S(t,s)≤√(B(t)B(s)) then proves finiteness for d≥3, with strict positivity near (0,0). Independently expanding J₀(4κt sin(θ/2)) through θ⁴ gives moments 2u² and 6u⁴+2u², u=κt. Cauchy–Schwarz above u² yields probability ≥1/8; both outer tails are ≤1/32 each when R≤u≤2R. Thus each disjoint ℓ∞ annulus at R=32^j contributes at least a positive constant times κ⁻². With reset, retain R≤κ/r where exp(-rt)≥exp(-2) on those intervals, giving the stated logarithmic lower bound. Integrating B with the exponential weight and splitting κt at 1 and κ/r yields O(κ⁻¹ log²(κ/r)); squaring gives the planar upper bound. The exact one-dimensional Fourier multiplier r/√(r²+16κ²sin²(θ/2)) gives Q₁ by Parseval and a tangent substitution. The absolute difference of two independent Exp(r) ages is Exp(r), giving the stated purity integral. Averaging the J₀ addition identity gives the elliptic transform with complementary modulus r/√(r²+16κ²), hence the logarithm. The origin-neighbor matrix element is -ir(1-P_d)/(4dκ) by integration by parts and |J₀(x)|<1 for x>0; its squared modulus contributes to the strict off-diagonal gap. Dominated convergence gives P_d/r→M_d for d≥3 and hence the stated ratio. Source checker inspected, not executed: its 55 finite assertions concern truncated quadrature and algebra; the witness is sampled at five d values {1,2,3,4,6}, not at d=5. Neither the checker nor the theorem gives an exact planar equivalent.

evidence: Wald–Böttcher give the general finite-network exponential age integral and Hamiltonian-basis resolvent; on regular lattices the Laplacian differs from hopping by shift and scale. Their finite-N expression neither controls the infinite lattice nor supplies the weak-reset ℓ² threshold.

Das–Dattagupta–Gupta give the exact same stationary 1D profile at Δ=2κ, λ=r, reset site 0; its Fourier form immediately produces Q₁ by Parseval. Acharya–Gupta give the same free 1D Bessel kernel but study conditional resetting.
broader_coverage.reasoning: General resolvent/age formulas and the exact site law are prior starting points. An estimate integrable in time for d≥3 alone would still not prove sharpness; the annular estimate giving the 2D obstruction is not an immediate finite-network corollary.

evidence: Substituting the lattice kernel into Eq. (34)'s age formalism gives the starting site law, and the 1D case can be obtained directly from Eq. (52). The two-time overlap uses products of diagonal site probabilities at two distinct ages; integrating the squared return amplitude at their difference instead gives P_d.

The prior coherent weak-reset hierarchy fixes the numerator of P_d/Q_d, not its denominator. For d≥3, the 1/r ratio is an immediate consequence once the independent diagonal criterion with positive C_d is proved.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Neither prior equality of full density matrices nor availability of the general resolvent is a stronger theorem about spatial collision convergence. A genuine stronger mixed-norm/dispersive theorem for the same kernel would be coverage; none was identified in the inspected passages.

value.rationale: A pair of independent positions from the reset stationary state gives a directly defined collision statistic, distinct from a quantum-state purity measurement. The theorem pins down the dimension at which its renormalized coefficient is finite and shows that in higher dimensions coherence dominates it by an inverse-rate factor. The exact dimension threshold depends on both upper and critical lower estimates; it is not mere evaluation of the known ensemble return integral.
